title: THE ESA STANDARD FOR TELEMETRY & TELECOMMAND PACKET UTILISATION P.U.S.
short_title: The ESA Packet Utilisation Standard (PUS) paper
status_notes: Historical conference paper. It describes the PUS as approved by the ESA Inspector General after a review during 1993, and therefore an Agency standard, and expects it to evolve incrementally (PDF p. 6). It cites the PUS as ESA PSS-07-101 Issue 1, May 1994 (PDF p. 6).

key_points.text: ESA's packet telemetry and telecommand standards, derived from CCSDS recommendations, cover end-to-end transfer between ground applications and on-board Application Processes but leave open the internal structure and content of packets; the PUS addresses this.
An Application Process is a logical on-board entity that generates TM packets and receives TC packets, uniquely identified by an Application ID used for the end-to-end connection with the ground.

The production of the PUS was the responsibility of the ESA Committee for Operations and EGSE Standards (COES), set up in 1987 to define functions common to satellite checkout (EGSE) and satellite control systems.

The PUS contains operational requirements, standards for the secondary data header of TM and TC packets, a set of PUS Services (on-board service model plus full definition of the service data units), and standards for data structures and parameter encoding types.

The Packet Data Field Header carries the Service Type and Service Subtype; up to 256 services and 256 subtypes per service, with 0-127 reserved for the PUS and 128-255 mission-specific. The TM and TC headers are identical except that a TM packet may carry an optional time field.
The header version number allows future versions, for example packets with multiple Service Data Units as proposed by NASA/JPL for deep-space missions.

17 PUS Services were then defined: 1 Telecommand Verification, 2 Device Command Distribution, 3 Housekeeping & Diagnostic Data Reporting, 4 Statistical Data Reporting, 5 Event Reporting, 6 Memory Management, 7 Task Management, 8 Function Management, 9 Time Management, 10 Time Packet, 11 On-Board Scheduling, 12 On-board Monitoring, 13 Large Data Transfer, 14 Packet Transmission Control, 15 On-Board Storage and Retrieval, 16 On-Board Traffic Management, 17 Test.

No PUS service is mandatory, but all Application Processes are expected to implement Telecommand Verification; verification can cover acceptance, start, intermediate stages and completion, selectable per command, with positive and/or negative acknowledgements.

Device Command Distribution has three sub-services: distribution at TC Segment level (needing no software, e.g. to unblock or reset the Packet Assembly Controller), CPDU high-priority on/off pulses, and distribution by other Application Processes, e.g. over an internal bus.

Housekeeping packets can be defined or redefined in flight, and an optional event-driven mode generates a packet only when a parameter changes by more than a threshold; a diagnostic sub-service supports high sampling rates for troubleshooting.

On-Board Scheduling allows loading, deleting, reporting and controlling the release status of telecommands, time-shifting them, and interlocking a telecommand to the success or failure of an earlier one.

Large Data Transfer moves a large Service Data Unit (e.g. a file or large memory load) in a sequence of smaller packets, uplink or downlink; Storage and Retrieval may use several stores, and storing all event-driven packets gives a 'lost packet recovery' capability.
The Test service includes a standard Link Test ('Are you alive?') sub-service.

Tailoring: missions implement only the services and sub-services they need; mission-optional fields linked to unused capability sets can be omitted; the PUS specifies only the encoding type of each field, its length being fixed at mission level.

The standard was validated by the PUSV prototype on SPARC workstations with the PUSSAT reference satellite model (completed 1992) and approved by the ESA Inspector General after a review in 1993; ESOC's SCOS-II will give full application-level support to PUS missions.
